findings.title: Type the extracted generation function
findings.description: PROJECT_RULES.md R-12 says: "Python functions must carry type hints on parameters and return values, and must not use bare `except:` or `except Exception: pass`." This new function leaves `set_status` untyped and has no return annotation, so callers and maintainers cannot check the callback or returned tuple contract. Verification: `git show HEAD:PROJECT_RULES.md` confirmed R-12; `git show HEAD:src-tauri/sidecar/server.py | nl -ba | sed -n '290,299p'` confirmed the signature lacks those annotations.

findings.title: Cover queued generation status transitions
findings.description: The extraction moves progress updates into a callback passed to the queued generation function, but the sidecar integration tests only cover invalid generation requests and unknown IDs; they do not enqueue a successful or failing job and observe its status. If this callback is omitted or stops updating the record, generation can finish while clients continue polling `queued` until timeout. Add a focused queue/status test (using a controlled generation function) that verifies progress and terminal success/error states for the reworked lifecycle.

findings.title: Model commands bypass the shared sidecar HTTP client
findings.description: The new managed client is consumed by commands in local_tts.rs and by pipeline.rs, but the existing model commands in models.rs still construct a fresh reqwest client for each /models/status and /models/download call. That leaves sidecar HTTP ownership split across two patterns, so those requests bypass the registered connection pool and the per-request timeout helper. Have the model commands use the managed HttpClient and the shared timeout helper so all Rust sidecar calls follow the same boundary.

findings.title: Timeout ends before the response body is read
findings.description: This timeout wraps only `RequestBuilder::send()`, which returns once the response headers arrive. The shared client has no default timeout, so later body reads such as `response.bytes().await` in `get_generation_audio` (and `text()`/`json()` elsewhere) can wait indefinitely if the sidecar stalls while streaming a response. Apply the deadline through body consumption as well, or configure a request timeout that covers the complete response.

findings.title: Add boundary coverage for generated audio fetch
findings.description: The new Tauri command is the only path by which the webview now retrieves generated audio, but the added frontend test only mocks the command and checks for a `blob:` URL and invocation. No test exercises this command's HTTP response handling or verifies that returned bytes are preserved, and the helper tests cover only ID validation. A regression that returns an error for a successful response, mishandles bytes, or fails to propagate a sidecar HTTP error would therefore leave the new audio flow unguarded.

findings.title: Audio fetch timeout stops at response headers
findings.description: If the sidecar sends audio response headers and then stalls while streaming the WAV, this timeout has already completed; the following `response.bytes().await` can wait indefinitely. The shared client has no default timeout, whereas the old per-call client timeout covered reading the response body, so the new audio command can hang instead of failing after 30 seconds.

findings.title: Test concurrent sidecar startup notification path
findings.description: This replaces the previous polling wait with notification and timeout behavior, but the modified Rust tests cover only default state and port helpers; none exercise two callers arriving during startup, startup completion/failure notification, or the timeout path. Those are the branches that ensure concurrent pipeline requests reuse one startup and receive its result, so a missed wakeup or incorrect error path could regress startup without a test failing.

findings.title: Generated audio URL is not released when the route unmounts
findings.description: This revokes the previous generated audio only when another generation starts. `getAudioUrl()` now creates a `blob:` URL for the generated WAV, but navigating away from the wizard leaves the latest URL unreleased; repeated visits can retain large audio blobs for the lifetime of the webview. Revoke the current generated URL during component teardown as well.
